$comment: Tier-B inventory for scripts/production-artefact-check.js (S-E06-1 / PF-54).
Each entry is a COUNT of `?? 'scheme://localhost…'` configuration fallbacks still
present in that file. They are real instances of PF-54 — 'development URLs ship in
production-facing code' — that this slice deliberately did NOT fix: removing them
touches nine web call sites and three worker/api ones with a genuine local-dev
regression risk, which is a different change from the four rendered Maildev copies
and the credential fallbacks that S-E06-1 does close.
This is an inventory, not an amnesty. The ratchet fails in BOTH directions: above a
count (debt added), below a count (lower it — a ratchet that never tightens is a
rubber band), and on any file with a hit that is absent from this list (no escape by
omission). `--update` refuses to write while any Tier-A rule fires, so a broken tree
can never be frozen in here.
Measured 2026-08-04: 17 fallbacks across 16 files, after S-E06-1 removed the two in
keycloak-admin.service.ts and jwt.strategy.ts.
Follow-up is PF-54, which stays OPEN for exactly these 17 — not S-E06-2, which is CSP
and branding injection (PF-45) and has nothing to do with them. Corrected by run 18;
the original note pointed at the wrong story.
